skill.name: verify-and-stop
skill.description: Prove existing work meets acceptance conditions without expanding scope. Use for validation-only tasks, completion checks, focused gate runs, and last-mile proof.
skill.summary: Validate acceptance conditions with focused evidence, report unresolved risks, and stop when proof is complete.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The skill contains only instructions and metadata, with no executable code or suspicious static findings. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or business logic abuse was found.

content.value_statement: Verification tasks often expand into unnecessary edits and broad testing. This skill selects focused evidence, reports exact outcomes, and stops when acceptance is proven.
actual_capabilities: Translates acceptance conditions into a focused proof set.
Reuses current results when they match the repository state.
Prioritizes focused checks before broader validation gates.
Separates passed, failed, unavailable, and blocked outcomes.
Reports commands, results, and unresolved risks.
Stops once the requested acceptance proof is complete.
limitations: It does not define acceptance criteria that the user has not provided.
It cannot guarantee correctness beyond the checks and evidence available.
It does not edit product code unless the request explicitly includes fixes.
It avoids unrelated cleanup, polish, and additional tests.

use_cases.title: Confirm a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Run the smallest relevant checks and report whether a submitted fix meets its stated acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Check required release gates, distinguish unavailable checks, and summarize remaining risks without expanding scope.

use_cases.title: Review Delivered Work
use_cases.description: Compare completed work with acceptance conditions and produce concise evidence for each result.

prompt_templates.title: Verify One Criterion
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this acceptance criterion: [criterion]. Run the smallest sufficient check, report the result, and stop.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused confirmation for one requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Completed Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that [completed task] satisfies these criteria: [criteria]. Reuse current evidence when valid, then run only missing checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs evidence that finished work meets several conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Run Focused Release Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate [release or change] against [required gates]. Start with focused checks, expand only when necessary, and classify every outcome precisely.
prompt_templates.scenario: A release manager needs efficient gate validation before approval.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Auditable Proof Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Map each acceptance condition for [change] to the smallest reliable proof. Execute applicable checks and report commands, results, gaps, and unresolved risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced reviewer needs traceable evidence across complex acceptance conditions.

output_examples.input: Verify that the login error message appears for invalid credentials.
output_examples.output: Pass. The focused authentication test confirmed the expected error message for invalid credentials. No broader checks were needed.

output_examples.input: Confirm the release passes the required lint and unit test gates.
output: Lint: Pass. The configured lint command completed without errors.
Unit tests: Unavailable. The required test dependency is missing.
Unresolved risk: Unit test status remains unverified.

output_examples.input: Check whether the documented acceptance criteria are satisfied.
output_examples.output: Blocked. No acceptance criteria were provided, so a reliable proof set cannot be selected.

best_practices: Keep the repository state stable while existing results are reused.
Request fixes separately when verification identifies a failure.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad improvements during a validation-only task.
Do not treat unavailable checks as passed checks.
Do not continue testing after sufficient acceptance evidence is complete.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies existing work against acceptance conditions supplied in the request.

faq.question: Will it modify product code?
faq.answer: No. It modifies code only when the verification request explicitly includes fixes.

faq.question: How does it choose checks?
faq.answer: It selects the smallest reliable proof set and runs focused checks before broader gates.

faq.question: Can it reuse previous test results?
faq.answer: Yes. Results can be reused when they remain current and match the repository state.

faq.question: How are incomplete checks reported?
faq.answer: Each result is classified as passed, failed, unavailable, or blocked, with unresolved risk stated clearly.

faq.question: When does verification stop?
faq.answer: It stops when the available evidence sufficiently proves every requested acceptance condition.
